significance: A sandstone yogini temple at Badoh with a rectangular shrine under a tall massive shikhara, forty-two niches for goddess images and seven subsidiary shrines around it; eighteen of the broken goddess figures that once sat in its grooves survive. It is compared with the Teli ka Mandir at Gwalior and now holds both Hindu and Jain images.
story: Locals hold that the temple was raised by shepherds, gadariya, which is how it came by the name Gadarmal.
